sentences.text: Sunlight looks white, but it is made of many colors traveling together.
A rainbow can appear when that light meets raindrops in the air.
The light enters a drop, bends, and spreads into its colors.
Inside the drop, the light bounces off the back, then bends again as it comes out.
Each color leaves at a slightly different angle, which is why we see bands.
On the main bow, red is on the outside and violet is on the inside.
To see a rainbow, you need the sun behind you and the rain in front of you.
Your own shadow points toward the middle of the bow.
If the rain stops or the sun moves behind clouds, the rainbow can fade.
A second, fainter bow sometimes appears outside the first, with the colors reversed.
A rainbow is not a solid object you could touch. It is light reaching your eyes from many drops at once.
Two people standing apart may see the bow in slightly different places.

questions.prompt: What is this passage mostly about?

choices.text: How sunlight and raindrops make a rainbow
How to paint a solid arch in the sky
Why shadows are always red and violet
How two people can hold one rainbow

questions.explanation: The passage follows light into a raindrop, back out as separated colors, and explains where you must stand. That is the main idea.

questions.prompt: The light bends inside a raindrop. What does bends mean here?

choices.text: Turns the sun off for an hour

questions.explanation: Here, bends means changes direction. The light enters the drop and does not keep going in a straight line, so the colors can spread.

questions.prompt: Where is red on the main bow?

choices.text: On the inside, next to violet's place swapped
In the shadow at your feet
Only in the second, fainter bow

questions.explanation: The passage says that on the main bow, red is on the outside and violet is on the inside. The fainter bow reverses the colors.

questions.prompt: What happens to the light first?

choices.text: It bounces off the back of the drop
It leaves as separate color bands
It fades when the rain stops

questions.explanation: The path in the passage starts when light enters a drop. Bouncing and leaving come after that. Fading happens later, if the rain stops.
